projects.title: DocPulseAI - AI Platform for Code Intelligence
projects.summary: Built a repository intelligence platform that extracts APIs, entities, and dependencies from large codebases.
projects.description: DocPulseAI is a backend-focused platform for understanding complex repositories using AST-based analysis pipelines and service-oriented processing.
projects.focus: Code intelligence, backend services, cloud deployment
projects.problem: Large repositories are hard to understand quickly, especially when APIs and dependency relationships are spread across many modules.
goals: Extract structured intelligence (APIs, entities, dependencies) from real-world repositories.
Provide fast queryable outputs for developers exploring unfamiliar codebases.
Deploy an analysis pipeline that can scale beyond local scripts.
ownership: Designed and implemented AST parsing workflows using Tree-sitter.
Built service logic to extract APIs, entities, and dependency relationships from repository code.
Containerized services and productionized deployment workflows on Azure.
constraints: Needed to handle repositories with different code styles and architectural patterns.
Balanced depth of analysis with compute cost and response-time expectations.
architecture: Parser and extraction services process repositories into structured metadata.
Data and artifacts are persisted using PostgreSQL and Blob Storage.
Deployed a microservices setup on Azure ACA/ACR for reproducible environment management.
qualitySignals: Service boundaries reduced coupling between parsing, extraction, and storage concerns.
Containerized deployment made environment behavior consistent across runs.
Cloud persistence enabled repeatable analysis workflows instead of one-off scripts.
impact: Made codebase intelligence searchable and structured instead of manual and ad-hoc.
Improved developer onboarding and exploration speed for large repositories.
Delivered a cloud-ready deployment path for scaling analysis workloads.
challenges: Balancing parsing depth and processing performance for large repositories.
Keeping extracted relationships consistent across different code patterns.
nextSteps: Add language-agnostic extraction modules for multi-language monorepos.
Introduce ranking/relevance signals for faster API and dependency discovery.

projects.title: Edge Co-Intelligence System
projects.summary: Built a distributed edge inference system that parallelizes YOLOv8 detection across worker nodes with fault tolerance.
projects.description: This project focuses on low-latency computer vision inference by distributing workloads across multiple edge workers and aggregating predictions in real time.
projects.focus: Edge inference orchestration and low-latency backend design
projects.problem: Single-node inference pipelines become bottlenecks under high throughput and are fragile when a worker fails.
goals: Parallelize inference workloads across distributed worker nodes.
Keep end-to-end latency low while increasing throughput.
Maintain continuity when nodes fail or become unhealthy.
ownership: Designed orchestration logic for distributing inference jobs across worker nodes.
Implemented health checks, retries, and failure recovery for resilient processing.
Built aggregation and response pipelines for real-time inference output.
constraints: Needed to coordinate variable worker performance and intermittent availability.
Real-time output required strict handling of response order and retries.
architecture: Controller routes inference requests to workers based on availability and load.
Workers run YOLOv8 inference and stream outputs for centralized aggregation.
Fault-tolerant logic handles retries and worker failover without stopping the full pipeline.
qualitySignals: Health-aware scheduling reduced avoidable failures from unstable workers.
Retry and failover strategy improved system resilience under node churn.
Streaming aggregation maintained usable real-time behavior under load.
impact: Improved throughput by parallelizing inference workloads across multiple workers.
Reduced single-point-of-failure risk with health monitoring and retry strategy.
Enabled stable real-time detection under variable worker availability.
challenges: Managing worker coordination while keeping latency predictable.
Handling node failures without creating duplicate or dropped inference results.
nextSteps: Add autoscaling policies based on queue depth and latency thresholds.
Introduce observability dashboards for worker-level performance diagnostics.

projects.title: Quizora AI - Online Assessment Platform
projects.summary: Developed a stateless assessment API with secure role-based access control and automated grading flows.
projects.description: Quizora AI is an online assessment platform centered on secure backend workflows for quiz creation, assignment, evaluation, and access control.
projects.focus: Secure API design, assessment workflow automation, RBAC
projects.problem: Assessment systems need secure multi-role workflows while keeping quiz creation, delivery, and grading consistent at scale.
goals: Support end-to-end quiz lifecycle for faculty and students.
Ensure secure role-based access to all sensitive operations.
ownership: Built stateless REST APIs in Spring Boot with transactional quiz lifecycle flows.
Implemented secure authentication and authorization with Spring Security and JWT.
Designed faculty and student RBAC paths for controlled access to sensitive operations.
constraints: Assessment data integrity had to be preserved across assignment and grading flows.
Authorization boundaries needed to be strict without blocking valid faculty workflows.
architecture: Spring Boot services expose APIs for quiz management, assignment, and grading.
MySQL stores users, quizzes, attempts, and evaluation state with transactional consistency.
JWT-based security layer enforces role-based access at API boundaries.
qualitySignals: Transactional operations protected consistency in quiz distribution and scoring.
RBAC checks at API level reduced privilege misuse risk.
Stateless auth model simplified horizontal scaling behavior.
impact: Enabled secure and role-aware access to all assessment workflows.
Reduced manual grading effort through automated result processing.
Kept backend stateless for easier scaling and deployment.
challenges: Designing role boundaries that are strict but still practical for faculty workflows.
Maintaining transactional integrity across quiz distribution and grading operations.
nextSteps: Add audit trails for faculty-side content updates and grading overrides.
Expand analytics endpoints for cohort performance insights.

projects.title: SnapDish - Food Delivery Platform
projects.summary: Built a full-stack food delivery platform with order lifecycle management and admin analytics capabilities.
projects.description: SnapDish combines customer-facing ordering flows with operational tooling for restaurants and administrators using a robust REST backend.
projects.focus: Order lifecycle APIs, operations dashboards, data aggregation
projects.problem: Food delivery platforms require dependable order-state transitions and real-time operational visibility for restaurants and admins.
goals: Implement reliable order lifecycle transitions across user and admin flows.
Support restaurant discovery and order operations through clean API contracts.
Provide dashboard-friendly data for operational visibility.
ownership: Implemented backend APIs for restaurants, orders, and lifecycle state transitions.
Built admin workflows for order monitoring and revenue-level insights.
Connected frontend user journeys to backend business logic with consistent API contracts.
constraints: Needed to prevent inconsistent order states during high activity windows.
Dashboard and transactional APIs had competing read/write performance demands.
architecture: Express services manage business logic for ordering, tracking, and restaurant operations.
MongoDB supports operational data access patterns for both customer and admin views.
API aggregation endpoints power dashboard-level reporting requirements.
qualitySignals: Lifecycle-driven APIs reduced state mismatches between client and server.
Aggregation endpoints simplified dashboard data fetching and reduced client complexity.
Backend contract consistency improved maintainability across product surfaces.
impact: Streamlined order operations across customer and admin experiences.
Improved operational visibility through analytics-oriented endpoints.
Maintained consistent lifecycle handling to reduce state mismatches.
challenges: Coordinating multiple order states without race-condition style inconsistencies.
Keeping dashboard reporting responsive with growing operational data.
nextSteps: Add event-driven notifications for restaurant and delivery state changes.
Introduce caching for high-frequency dashboard queries.

projects.title: Air Quality Forecasting System
projects.summary: Built an AQI forecasting pipeline and benchmarked models to improve predictive performance.
projects.description: This project applies machine learning to air quality prediction, combining data analysis and model comparison to optimize AQI forecasting quality.
projects.focus: Regression modeling, feature analysis, model serving
projects.problem: AQI trends are influenced by multiple pollutants, making accurate forecasting difficult without careful model and feature selection.
goals: Identify high-signal pollutant features for AQI prediction.
Benchmark model families and select the most reliable performer.
Serve predictions through an API-ready backend workflow.
ownership: Conducted EDA to identify high-signal pollutant relationships.
Benchmarked regression algorithms and selected Random Forest as best performer.
Packaged model inference into a Flask-based serving workflow.
constraints: Model performance needed to generalize instead of fitting only historical patterns.
Serving pipeline had to remain simple enough for practical integration.
architecture: Data preprocessing and feature engineering pipeline feeds candidate models.
Model evaluation workflow compares algorithms using consistent validation criteria.
Flask endpoint serves AQI predictions for application-level consumption.
qualitySignals: Model evaluation pipeline ensured like-for-like comparisons across algorithms.
Feature analysis reduced noise and improved interpretability of predictions.
API-based serving made the model usable beyond notebook experimentation.
impact: Achieved an R² score of 87% with Random Forest.
Improved model reliability by grounding feature selection in EDA findings.
Made forecasting usable through an API-oriented serving layer.
challenges: Avoiding overfitting while optimizing for higher predictive accuracy.
Translating offline model performance into a practical serving workflow.
nextSteps: Add periodic retraining with fresh environmental data.
Track model drift and confidence bands in prediction responses.
